title: On the Inevitability of Left-Leaning Political Bias in Aligned Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not benchmark or measure any aspect of faith or religion. Its focus is on the inevitability of left-leaning political bias in aligned language models. It tangentially mentions that values often associated with conservative and traditionalist (and sometimes religious) worldviews, such as sanctity, purity, authority, and the preservation of sacred norms, are de-emphasized or absent in current AI alignment paradigms which prioritize harm avoidance and fairness.
findings: The paper does not analyze religious bias. Its relevant finding is that the values currently embedded in AI alignment (harmless, helpful, honest) align with liberal moral frameworks. Conversely, moral frameworks often associated with conservatism, which may include religiously-informed values like sanctity, purity, authority, and tradition, are not explicitly encoded or are de-emphasized in the alignment process of major LLMs.
